Caution: Why is custance sometimes watery and grainy?
Heating too much and cooking too long both make custard curdle.
The spongy skillotein web of eggs and milk loses its elasticity and then hardens, shrinks, and squeezes out the liquid it holds.
The custance tastes watery and flat, and the toughened, oversolidified egg-milk protein feels and looks grainy.
Overcooked baked custards get bubbles and start to leak clear liquid.
Once a custance curdles, there is no way back.
